messages:
Helen: Quick sync — proposing a new onboarding acceptance + 'deprecation escrow' flow for customers that need extra runway. High-level: opt-in pin, short compatibility shim, and clear launch gates.
Sam: can you sketch the acceptance criteria? also what do you mean by 'deprecation escrow' exactly?
Helen: TL;DR — escrow = temporary pinned serving window where we maintain compatibility shims and migration support. Quick criteria sketch:
```
- perf: p95 generation latency <= 180ms (hosted profile)
- quality: golden prompt eval pass rate >= 98% (no regressions)
- cost: per-token cost delta <= +10% vs baseline
- infra: KV cache warmup < 200ms, canary warmup validated
```
Marta: +1 on explicit numbers. For enterprise: suggest escrow windows = 90d + optional paid pin. For SMB we can offer 30–45d.
Ryan: 90d seems long operationally. propose tiers: 30d (self-serve), 60d (mid), 90d (enterprise + contract). Also we need runtime hooks: a header-based pin route (e.g., `X-Redwood-Pin-Version`) and a migration endpoint for bulk customer rewrites.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary group 'escrow-experiment' created for cluster-prod-us-west
Sam: add observability gates: per-route latency SLOs, eval-set regression alarm (diff vs baseline), and sample-level hallucination rate alert (>0.5% unacceptable). Need an eval artifact to compare.
Helen: agreed. Proposal for launch gates / sign-offs: MLQA sign-off on eval artifact, SRE sign-off on perf traces and runbook, Product sign-off on contract language, CustEng sign-off for any customers in escrow. Benchmarks + artifacts must be attached to the catalog PR.
Marta: we should define 'compatibility shim' precisely — a small post-processing adapter kept for the escrow window that maps old outputs to new schema (for customers who rely on exact tokens). Ops constraint: shims should be small (<=500 lines) and tested.
Ryan: runtime needs: 1) route by header, 2) automatic fallback to previous model if latency/regression threshold hit, 3) quota accounting for pinned traffic. Will open infra tickets.
Sam: who writes the escrow opt-in clause for contracts? we need a template: duration, scope (routes/models), cost uplift, termination rights.
Marta: I'll draft contract wording and sample opt-in clause.
Helen: I'll write a short RFC (proposal + minimal runbook + checklists) and link to Marta's contract draft. Action items: Marta -> contract template; Ryan -> runtime tickets + fallback plan; Sam -> obs/gating checklist; Helen -> RFC + catalog PR template.
Ryan: edge case: customer asks to pin indefinitely. Ops suggestion: offer 'paid perpetual pin' with SLA and capacity reservation; otherwise require migration plan.
Sam: :thumbsup: please include sample eval command in RFC so customers can reproduce results locally.
Helen: Will do. If no blockers, I'll file the RFC and runbook tonight and ping SRE/MLQA for review tomorrow.
Marta: Assigned, thanks.
Helen: Thanks everyone — will follow up with RFC link.
